learning: If line_loss_events on s-bend and slalom fall and max_error drops, forward look-ahead was the gap. If line-loss stays at about 1.1 to 1.3 with max_error near 0.06 m, forward position is not the limit and the next test is turn authority (narrower wheel_track) or weights.
notes: Builder's iteration 4 geometry (iteration 1 best with sensor y moved to 0.07 m) paired with the unchanged iteration 1 controller, so only forward position differs from the best-known result.
rationale: The Builder's candidate is the iteration 1 geometry (best score 337.5) with the sensor row moved forward from y = 0.06 m to y = 0.07 m. Span stays at ±0.03 m, spacing 0.015 m, footprint 0.012 m, wheel_track 0.11 m, mass 0.7 kg and wheel_radius 0.03 m. Evidence: iteration 1 finished 13/20 oval runs at 1.83 s, so speed is not the limit. Its s-bend and slalom failures were all off-track exits at max_error about 0.062 to 0.063 m, with 1.1 to 1.3 line-loss events per run. Iteration 2 (wider span) and iteration 3 (0.016 m footprint) both scored lower, so neither span nor footprint is the lever. Forward position is the one geometry lever not yet tested alone. The controller is kept exactly as in iteration 1 (kp 2.5, ki 0, kd 0.3, base_speed 1.2, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2], last_direction), so any change in results is attributable to the forward move. Oval steering_oscillation of about 0.31 is a weight question, and I am deliberately not changing weights in this race so the forward-position test stays clean. Expected result, not yet measured: line-loss on s-bend and slalom falls toward 0.5 to 1.0 per run, max_error drops below about 0.055 m, and the oval finish rate holds near 13/20.
